title: Mapping Australia's Power System: Where the Transition Is Taking Shape
summary: A spatial view of Australia's electricity transition, from national generation growth to the state, technology and network constraints beneath it.
key_takeaway: Australia's next unit of transition value will increasingly come from connecting and coordinating renewable assets, not merely counting them.

inline_figures.caption: Total Australian electricity generation rises over the long run, so cleaner supply must replace existing output while serving a larger system.
A recent-accreditation snapshot maps installed renewable capacity and makes the concentration of new development visible.
Installed wind and solar capacity in the source sample varies sharply by state.
Wind supplies about two-thirds and solar about one-third of capacity in the recent-accreditation sample.
